$comment: Operational taxonomic units used as columns in the muscle occurrence tables. `rank` is informal. `path` gives the nesting used to build the phylogenetic sort order and the indentation in the UI; it is a pragmatic consensus topology, not a formal analysis. Note that Abdala & Diogo (2010) place Testudines as archosauromorphs sister to Crocodylia + Aves; that placement is followed here.

taxa.label: Hagfishes
taxa.notes: Cyclostome outgroup. Included chiefly for cranial/branchial muscle polarity.

taxa.label: Lampreys
taxa.notes: Agnathan outgroup for cranial muscles; lacks paired appendages, so appendicular rows are structurally absent rather than lost.

taxa.label: Cartilaginous fishes
taxa.notes: Plesiomorphic gnathostome condition for paired-appendage muscles: undivided dorsal (levator/extensor) and ventral (depressor/flexor) fin masses.

taxa.label: Ray-finned fishes
taxa.notes: Polypterus is the exemplar for appendicular muscles as the plesiomorphic extant actinopterygian (Diogo et al. 2016); Lepisosteus for branchial/cucullaris development (Naumann et al. 2017). Each paired fin has six muscles — the five-muscle gnathostome set plus the postaxial pterygialis caudalis.

taxa.label: Coelacanth
taxa.notes: Sister group to Dipnoi + Tetrapoda. Long excluded from fins-to-limbs discussion on the grounds that dipnoans are phylogenetically closer to tetrapods — which Diogo et al. (2016) argue was a mistake, because the dipnoan pectoral fin is secondarily simplified while Latimeria retains the plesiomorphic sarcopterygian condition. 14 of its pectoral muscles have one-to-one topological correspondences with pelvic muscles.

taxa.label: Lungfishes
taxa.notes: Closest extant sarcopterygian outgroup to tetrapods. The pectoral fin has only five muscles, but this is a derived dipnoan simplification, not the ancestral condition — the pelvic fin retains 25. Reading tetrapod ancestry off the lungfish pectoral fin therefore understates the ancestral complexity.

taxa.label: Stem tetrapodomorphs
taxa.notes: Muscle reconstructions are inferences from osteological correlates bracketed by Dipnoi and Amphibia (Molnar et al. 2018; Molnar & Diogo 2021). Treat all entries as hypotheses, not observations.

taxa.label: Salamanders
taxa.notes: Primary extant proxy for the plesiomorphic tetrapod limb muscle bauplan in Abdala & Diogo (2010) and Diogo & Molnar (2014).

taxa.label: Frogs and toads
taxa.notes: Highly derived limb musculature. Digit-1 loss shifts 'pollicis' muscles onto digit 2 — the standard example of positional rather than identity-based attachment.

taxa.label: Turtles
taxa.notes: Carapace rigidly links axial skeleton and girdle, and several axio-appendicular muscles are absent as discrete units. Cranial data follow Werneburg (2011).

taxa.label: Lizards, snakes, tuatara
taxa.notes: Most densely sampled reptilian group in Abdala & Diogo (2010) (>50 squamate species).

taxa.label: Stem pseudosuchians
taxa.notes: Large-bodied loricatan pseudosuchians outside Crocodylomorpha — the 'rauisuchian' grade. Liparini & Schultz (2013) reconstruct the thigh musculature of Prestosuchus under Witmer's inference levels and state them explicitly, which is why entries here carry the level in the occurrence note. Hypotheses, not observations.

taxa.label: Stem crocodylomorphs
taxa.notes: Gracile, long-limbed, erect-postured crocodylomorphs outside crown Crocodylia — the sphenosuchian grade. Muscle entries are inferences from osteological correlates bracketed by Crocodylia and Aves (Sues et al. 2003 for Dromicosuchus grallator, UNC 15574). Treat all entries as hypotheses, not observations. Correlates shared by both brackets are level I inferences; crocodylian-only correlates are level II' and should say so in the occurrence note. Note that these animals are gracile and erect-limbed, so scar development need not match the sprawling caimans most correlate maps are drawn from.

taxa.label: Stem crocodyliforms
taxa.notes: Notosuchian crocodyliforms — inside Crocodylomorpha, outside crown Crocodylia, and roughly 130 Myr younger than the sphenosuchian grade, which is why they are a separate column rather than folded into [[crocodylomorph-stem]]. Godoy et al. (2016) label muscle scars directly on the described bones. Hypotheses, not observations.

taxa.label: Crocodilians
taxa.notes: Extant phylogenetic bracket partner (with Aves) for archosaur fossil muscle reconstruction.

taxa.label: Birds
taxa.notes: The single conspicuous departure from the conservative tetrapod forelimb pattern; the flight apparatus reorganises the pectoral and antebrachial musculature.

taxa.label: Stem synapsids
taxa.notes: Muscle reconstructions bracketed by Reptilia and Mammalia (Bishop & Pierce 2024). Hypotheses, not observations.

taxa.label: Monotremes
taxa.notes: Retains a reptile-like pectoral girdle (coracoid, interclavicle) with mammalian muscle differentiation — the key intermediate for reading synapsid pectoral evolution (Gambaryan et al. 2015).

taxa.label: Marsupials and placentals
taxa.notes: Reference terminal for most clinical/veterinary muscle names. Rattus is the mammalian column in Diogo & Molnar (2014).
